pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How can you make the brightest part of a charcoal drawing? (1 mark)
   A. Smudge with a wet cloth
   B. Press very hard
   C. Leave the paper white or lift charcoal with a clean eraser
   D. Colour it black

2. Which is true about netball skills? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody needs to move
   B. Only shooters need to catch
   C. Only the umpire needs to pass
   D. Passing and catching are needed by every player

3. Colour value means (1 mark)
   A. how light or dark a colour is
   B. the price of a colour
   C. the smell of paint
   D. how loud a colour is

4. Which shows neatness in a montage? (1 mark)
   A. Loose pieces
   B. Torn edges
   C. Glue everywhere
   D. Clean cut edges and no glue marks

5. Where can you get pictures for a montage? (1 mark)
   A. From the sky
   B. Only from the bank
   C. From a rock
   D. Old newspapers and magazines

6. What is a critique? (1 mark)
   A. A rude remark
   B. An honest, kind talk about someone's work
   C. A rest
   D. A kind of drum

7. How many beats does a crotchet last? (1 mark)
   A. Half
   B. Two
   C. Four
   D. One

8. The Kodaly hand sign for m is (1 mark)
   A. a sloping palm
   B. a flat palm held level
   C. a closed fist
   D. a wave

9. The sol-fa syllable m is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. mah
   B. moh
   C. may
   D. me

10. What makes ending on d good for a short melody? (1 mark)
   A. It is the highest note
   B. It sounds unfinished
   C. It is the loudest note
   D. It sounds finished and at rest

11. On the Kenyan flag, black stands for (1 mark)
   A. the sea
   B. the people of Kenya
   C. peace
   D. the land

12. Where should your hands be at the start? (1 mark)
   A. Just behind the start line
   B. Over the line
   C. Far in front of the line
   D. In your pockets

13. Why should the knees lift high when sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. To look funny
   B. To give a stronger, longer stride
   C. To slow down
   D. To trip others

14. Which describes a false start in a sprint? (1 mark)
   A. Running in the wrong direction
   B. Moving before the last signal
   C. Finishing first
   D. Falling at the end

15. Why do we warm up before gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. To make the mat softer
   B. To learn songs
   C. To prepare the muscles and joints
   D. To make us tired

16. The East African Community is (1 mark)
   A. a river
   B. a group of countries in East Africa that work together
   C. a school
   D. a type of drum

17. A photograph is also called a (1 mark)
   A. stave
   B. drum
   C. photo
   D. montage

18. When you give feedback on a friend's photograph you should (1 mark)
   A. say what you like first and then suggest one improvement
   B. say nothing
   C. say it is terrible
   D. laugh

19. A subject in photography is (1 mark)
   A. the screen
   B. the battery
   C. the camera
   D. the person or thing you photograph

20. Where is the thumb hole? (1 mark)
   A. On the bell
   B. At the back
   C. Under the foot
   D. On the mouthpiece

21. How many lines are on a staff? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Ten
   C. Three
   D. Five

22. Why should you not use very hot water on a plastic recorder? (1 mark)
   A. It makes it heavier
   B. It makes it play higher
   C. It can bend the plastic
   D. It makes it louder

23. Why should recorders not be shared without cleaning? (1 mark)
   A. They become heavy
   B. They change colour
   C. Germs can spread through the mouthpiece
   D. They melt

24. Swimming is important because (1 mark)
   A. it replaces school
   B. it is a life skill that helps keep you safe near water
   C. it makes water disappear
   D. it needs no rules

25. In a glide, your arms are (1 mark)
   A. behind your back
   B. folded
   C. by your sides
   D. stretched above the head with palms together

26. In bubble blowing, you blow bubbles (1 mark)
   A. with soap
   B. on land only
   C. slowly in the water
   D. before you enter

27. Why do animal games often use singing or drumming? (1 mark)
   A. Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun
   B. To stop the game
   C. To hide the players
   D. To scare animals

28. Why are indigenous games part of our heritage? (1 mark)
   A. They were bought yesterday
   B. They have no meaning
   C. They are foreign
   D. They come to us from earlier generations

29. Why should you write the date on each work in your portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To spoil it
   C. For fun only
   D. To show when it was made

30. A portfolio is (1 mark)
   A. a song
   B. a ball
   C. a folder for keeping creative works together
   D. a kind of paint

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how partners should give feedback on each other's gymnastics. (3 marks)

32. Explain why it is dangerous for a child to jump into a river to rescue someone. (3 marks)

33. Explain the steps of a full sprint from the start commands to the finish. (5 marks)

34. Describe how to play the note G on the descant recorder and explain how to get a good tone. (5 marks)

35. Give three warm-up activities before sprinting. (3 marks)

36. Why should we take turns and respect others' views when talking about paintings and montages? (3 marks)

37. Why should you delete poor photographs from a device? (3 marks)

38. Describe the steps of a glide. (4 marks)

39. Why is it important not to share a recorder before cleaning it? (3 marks)

40. Name two types of songs learnt in this topic other than folk songs. (2 marks)

41. Describe how to paint a fruit so that it looks round using colour value. (4 marks)

42. What is a montage? (2 marks)

43. Write a melody that goes up by steps from d to m and comes down to d, and state the number of notes. (3 marks)

44. Give three examples of good etiquette during a performance. (3 marks)

45. Describe the game hawk and the chicks. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Leave the paper white or lift charcoal with a clean eraser
   The brightest parts have little or no charcoal.

2. D — Passing and catching are needed by every player
   Every player passes and catches during a game.

3. A — how light or dark a colour is
   Value is the lightness or darkness of a colour.

4. D — Clean cut edges and no glue marks
   Neatness means careful cutting and pasting.

5. D — Old newspapers and magazines
   Cut pictures from old papers and magazines.

6. B — An honest, kind talk about someone's work
   A critique gives fair comments in a respectful way.

7. D — One
   A crotchet lasts for one beat.

8. B — a flat palm held level
   Me is shown with a flat, level hand.

9. D — me
   The syllable m is me.

10. D — It sounds finished and at rest
   Ending on the home note gives a complete feeling.

11. B — the people of Kenya
   Black represents the people of Kenya.

12. A — Just behind the start line
   Hands go on the ground just behind the line.

13. B — To give a stronger, longer stride
   High knees produce a powerful stride.

14. B — Moving before the last signal
   A false start is leaving before the start signal.

15. C — To prepare the muscles and joints
   A warm body is less likely to be injured.

16. B — a group of countries in East Africa that work together
   The community brings countries together to cooperate.

17. C — photo
   Photo is short for photograph.

18. A — say what you like first and then suggest one improvement
   Kind and helpful feedback works best.

19. D — the person or thing you photograph
   The subject is what you are photographing.

20. B — At the back
   The left thumb covers the hole at the back.

21. D — Five
   The staff has five lines.

22. C — It can bend the plastic
   Heat can warp plastic.

23. C — Germs can spread through the mouthpiece
   Saliva can carry disease-causing germs.

24. B — it is a life skill that helps keep you safe near water
   Swimming helps prevent drowning.

25. D — stretched above the head with palms together
   Arms overhead create a streamlined shape.

26. C — slowly in the water
   You put your mouth in the water and blow out slowly.

27. A — Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun
   Music sets the pace.

28. D — They come to us from earlier generations
   Heritage is what we inherit.

29. D — To show when it was made
   Dates show how your skills grow.

30. C — a folder for keeping creative works together
   It protects and presents works.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watch carefully, say one good thing first, then one thing to improve, and be kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: The child may also drown because water can be deep or fast. It is safer to shout for an adult and throw something that floats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the danger, 2 marks for the safe action.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: On your marks: go to the line and take the position. Set: lift the hips slightly and stay still. Go: push hard and swing the arms. Run in your lane with high knees and bent arms. Keep running through the finish line and slow down gradually.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for marks, set, go, running technique and finishing.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: Hold the recorder with the left hand at the top and the right at the bottom. Cover the thumb hole and holes 1, 2 and 3 with the pads of the left fingers. Put the mouthpiece between the lips and blow gently and steadily with a soft too.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for holding, thumb hole, three holes, mouthpiece and gentle breath.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Jogging, arm circles, leg swings, gentle stretching, short easy strides. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is fair, it shows respect and it helps everyone learn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: To save memory space, keep only good pictures and make it easier to find the best ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stand with the back to the wall and arms stretched overhead. Put the feet on the wall and bend the knees. Take a breath and put the face in. Push off gently with the body straight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs from the mouth can spread illnesses such as colds through the mouthpiece.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for the mouth or mouthpiece, 1 mark for spreading illness.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sacred songs, patriotic songs and topical songs. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the outline. Paint the main colour. Add a lighter tone on the side facing the light and a darker tone on the side away from the light. Blend the edges and add a shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A picture made by joining many cut pictures or pieces of material on a background.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many pieces, 1 mark for joined on a background.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: d r m r d. There are five notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for going up, 1 mark for coming down, 1 mark for five.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk on and off quietly, listen to the leader, do not talk or laugh, clap for others, bow at the end. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: A hen stands in front and chicks hold on behind in a line. A hawk tries to tag the last chick. The hen spreads her arms and blocks. When the last chick is tagged, roles change.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid part.
